# Naga

> A simulation engine for Python, built on SimPy. A model is a JSON file of blocks, resources, stocks and flows, and agents; the engine runs it and returns statistics as pandas frames. Command `naga`, Python package `nagasim`.

Every page of the documentation, in the order of its menu. An agent that builds models should start with the model file format, the block reference and the agent tools.

The whole site as one file: llms-full.txt. Every page has a Markdown copy at its address with .md in place of .html.

## Start

- [Home](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/index.html): Naga is a simulation engine for Python, built on SimPy: you describe a system as a model file, and it runs the model and gives back an answer with its confidence interval.

## Learn

- [Learn Naga](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/learn/index.html): The learning path builds one model in six steps, and each page adds a few lines to the previous one and prints what the model does.
- [1. One queue](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/learn/1-one-queue.html): A queue with one server is the smallest model worth running, and the rest of this path grows it.
- [2. Two servers and a schedule](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/learn/2-two-servers-and-a-schedule.html): Real servers are not always there, so this step adds a second desk that is closed for the first four hours and open for the last four.
- [3. A tank level](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/learn/3-a-tank-level.html): A tank fills and drains continuously, which a queue model cannot say, so this step puts one in the same model.
- [4. Agents](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/learn/4-agents.html): An agent is a small statechart that lives in the model beside the blocks.
- [5. Replications and scenarios](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/learn/5-replications-and-scenarios.html): One run is one sample, so a claim about the model needs many runs and a comparison needs the same random numbers on both sides.
- [6. Reading the results](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/learn/6-results.html): Every run returns more than the headline number: summaries for each kind of component, and a log of what happened.

## By goal

- [How many replications, and what warm-up?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/replications-and-warm-up.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that finds how many replications a target precision needs, and how long a warm-up to set.
- [Which decision is best? Optimise it](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/optimise-a-decision.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that searches for the number of call-centre agents with the lowest daily cost.
- [Which inputs matter? Sensitivity and DOE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/sensitivity-and-doe.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that ranks three inputs of a call centre by how far they move the mean wait.
- [How do I fit input distributions from data?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/fit-input-distributions.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that fits candidate distributions to 200 handling times, picks the winner, and shows what the fit changes in a queue.
- [How sure am I, given my input data?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/input-uncertainty.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that reports a mean wait with two intervals, one from run-to-run noise and one that adds the input uncertainty of a distribution fitted to 30 observations.
- [How do I calibrate a model to data?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/calibrate-to-data.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that tunes the service rate of a one-server queue until the model's mean wait matches a measured 3.2 minutes.
- [How do I connect live data end to end?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/connect-live-data.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that reads a line's current rates from a web service on your own machine and writes them into a model.
- [How do I plan or schedule jobs?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/plan-or-schedule-jobs.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that sequences five jobs through a cutter and a packer with a solver, checks the plan by running it, and exports it for a planning system.
- [How do I import a Vensim or XMILE model?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/import-vensim-xmile.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that reads a small Vensim file into a model, lists what the reader could not translate, and checks the run against the closed-form answer.
- [How do I combine events, system dynamics and agents?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/hybrid-model.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that builds a help desk with tickets, a frustration stock and a staff team that takes breaks, then compares four and five staff.
- [How do I check a model in CI?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/check-in-ci.html): > In short > > - You build: a model file with three assertions, a naga check run that fails the build when one is false, and the workflow file that runs it on every push.
- [How do I cost a model and find the cost drivers?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/cost-drivers.html): > In short > > - You build: a script that prices a call centre's day and splits the total into agents busy, agents idle and callers waiting.
- [How do I drive a study from an AI agent?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/drive-a-study-from-an-ai-agent.html): > In short > > - You build: a short script that makes the tool calls an AI assistant makes: build a queue, run it, and ask what happens with a second server.
- [How do I share a viewer or a player?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/share-a-viewer-or-player.html): > In short > > - You build: a player file, one HTML page that replays a recorded run in a browser.
- [How do I write a plugin block?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/write-a-plugin-block.html): > In short > > - You build: a plugin file with one new block, INSPECT, and a model that uses it like a built-in block.
- [How do I train a policy with reinforcement learning?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/goals/train-a-policy-with-rl.html): > In short > > - You build: a policy for a routing decision, learned by reinforcement learning over many episodes, and judged against two simple rules.

## Learn

- [Glossary](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/glossary.html): This page defines the terms the learning path and the goal tutorials use, one line each.
- [Quick start from a model file](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/quickstart.html): A single-server queue, from nothing to numbers.
- [Tutorial: a log to a model in five minutes](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/event-log-tutorial.html): This page takes a real-looking event log from a job shop to a running model, and shows what to check before trusting it.

## Worked examples

- [Airport ground support](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/worked-examples/airport-ground-support.html): This page works through two decisions a ground handler at a hub faces: how many ramp agents and how much ground equipment a day's flight schedule needs, and whether that equipment can go electric and how it should charge.
- [Container terminal](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/worked-examples/container-terminal.html): This page works through two decisions a container terminal faces: whether to electrify the fleet that carries boxes between the quay and the yard, and how large a shore power connection at a berth should be.

## How-to

- [Compare scenarios and search](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/experiments.html): Everything about running more than one replication, comparing designs, and searching for a good one: nagasim.experiments (scenarios, CRN, precision, warm-up) and nagasim.optimize (DOE, ranking and selection, optimization), driven from the command line (naga scenarios, naga doe, naga optimize) or from Python.
- [Model assertions and CI](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/model-assertions.html): A model assertion pins one KPI against a comparison operator and value, checked over the model's own replications -- the same idea as a unit test, but for a simulation's steady-state behaviour instead of its code.
- [Semantic diff and merge](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/semantic-diff.html): A plain git diff on two model JSON files is mostly noise: a tool that saves a model writes blocks, resources and every other list back in whatever order its own structures hold them, so saving a model with no real edit can still produce a wall of reordered lines.
- [Share a model (the browser viewer)](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/sharing-a-model.html): A model can be shared as one HTML file in which the engine itself runs.
- [Event log to model](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/event-log-to-model.html): Most plants and offices already record what happened: which order went through which step, when it started and finished, and who did it.
- [From a SimPy script](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/simpy-script.html): A SimPy model you already have can become a Naga model without a rewrite.
- [Use from Python](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/python-api.html): The command line is a thin layer over a few functions.
- [Use with an agent](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/mcp.html): The engine has a set of tools an LLM agent calls to build, validate, run, debug and analyse a model: Agent tools lists every one.
- [Run a study with an assistant](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/ai-study.html): The engine can keep a whole simulation study in a folder and test every model step, so any assistant that speaks to it (see Use with an agent) can run a study without remembering anything between calls.
- [Pick tools with a small model](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/tool-picker.html): find_tool ranks the agent tools by plain word overlap, and a small re-ranking model can put the right tool first more often.

## Recipes (How do I...?)

- [Recipes: How do I...?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/index.html): Each recipe answers one modelling question with a tiny model, the output it prints and a short explanation.

## Service and repair times

- [How do I model handling times with an occasional very long one?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/lognormal-tail.html): Manual work is usually quick, with now and then a job that takes far longer.
- [How do I model a job made of several short steps?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/erlang-steps.html): A bake, a wash or an inspection often runs through a fixed number of steps in a row.
- [How do I model repair times with a long tail?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/repair-tail.html): Repair and lifetime data often have a heavier tail than a lognormal.
- [How do I model an approval or reaction time that is never negative?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/decision-delay.html): A person's reaction or an approval step takes time that is positive and skewed to the right.
- [How do I keep a skewed time between a minimum and a maximum?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/bounded-yield.html): A filling step can take at most 10 minutes and never less than 2, and it is usually closer to the top.
- [How do I use a histogram from a time study as a service time?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/histogram-times.html): A time study gives bins and the share of jobs in each, not a formula.
- [How do I model a time that is a fixed part plus a random part?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/formula-time.html): A repair is a fixed diagnosis followed by a random fix, and no single distribution says that.
- [How do I stop a cycle time from going negative?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/bounded-cycle.html): A normal cycle time has no floor, so a draw can fall below zero when the spread is large.
- [How do I model a correction time that grows with a positioning error?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/positioning-error.html): A robot that misses its target by some distance spends time putting it right.
- [What happens to a queue when service times have wild outliers?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/wild-outliers.html): Some data have extreme values on both sides, and the Cauchy distribution is the standard model of that.

## Failures and arrivals

- [How do I model a machine that wears out?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/weibull-wear-out.html): A machine that wears out fails at about the same age, while a memoryless machine fails at any age.
- [How do I run arrivals from a fixed timetable?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/timetable-arrivals.html): A delivery plan or a roster lists the exact times things arrive.

## Counts and chance

- [How do I model the number of lines on an order?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/poisson-lines.html): An order has a random number of lines, with a known average.
- [How do I count the defects in a batch?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/binomial-defects.html): A batch of parts holds a number of defective ones, each defective with the same chance.
- [How do I model retesting until a part passes?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/retest-attempts.html): A part is tested again until it passes, and each try costs the same time.
- [How do I model inspecting a sample from a finite lot?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/lot-sample.html): An inspector draws a small sample from a lot with a known number of defectives and does not put the parts back.
- [How do I draw order sizes from my own data?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/order-sizes.html): Order sizes are whole numbers, and you may know either their range or their measured shares.

## Delays, smoothing and forecasts

- [How do I add a first-order information delay to a forecast?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/forecast-lag.html): A planner's forecast follows demand but with a lag, because it averages what has been seen.
- [How do I delay goods in transit by a fixed time or a spread of times?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/transit-delay.html): Goods that leave on day 5 either all arrive exactly 4 days later, or arrive over a spread of days around the mean.
- [How do I smooth a noisy signal?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/smooth-noise.html): A daily reading jumps around, and a decision that follows it jumps too.
- [How do I extrapolate a growing trend?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/trend-forecast.html): Sales that grow steadily can be projected a few weeks ahead from their recent growth rate.

## Rates, tests and money

- [How do I add a daily or weekly cycle to a rate?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/daily-cycle.html): Demand, solar output and many flows swing over a day and drop at weekends.
- [How do I test a model with a step, a ramp and a pulse?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/test-inputs.html): Before you trust a model, push a known input through it and see how it answers.
- [How do I discount a stream of cash?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/discounted-cash.html): A plant that earns every year is worth less in today's money the later the cash arrives.
- [How do I stop a ratio dividing by zero?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/safe-ratio.html): A yield is good parts over parts made, and it is 0 over 0 until the line starts.
- [How do I turn a heading and a distance into x and y?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/bearing.html): A vehicle that flies a leg at a known heading ends up at an x and y offset, and you may need the heading back.

## Agents

- [How do I let an agent react to the agents near it?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/near-agents.html): A vehicle slows down when others are close, or a sensor reads the load of its neighbours.
- [How do I let an agent read the agents in the cells around it?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/neighbour-grid.html): On a grid, neighbours are the cells around you and not the agents within a distance.

## Flow blocks

- [How do I limit the work waiting between two machines?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/buffer-wip.html): A buffer between two machines holds a few parts.
- [How do I move parts along a belt?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/belt-transit.html): A belt delays each part by its length over its speed and holds only so many parts.
- [How do I turn one order into several jobs?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/order-copies.html): One customer order is often several tasks, such as three dishes.
- [How do I make two kinds of entity wait for each other?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/pair-flows.html): A ride needs a rider and a driver, and each waits until the other is there.
- [How do I pack parts on a pallet and unpack them later?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/unpack-pallet.html): Parts travel together on a pallet and are handled one by one at the end.
- [How do I route entities by a rule I write in Python?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/custom-routing.html): Chance and conditions cover most routing, but sometimes the rule is code.
- [How do I share a site's power limit between chargers?](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/how-to/recipes/site-power.html): A depot with a grid limit cannot give every car its full power at once.

## Digital twin

- [Digital twin](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/digital-twin.html): A digital twin is a model that reads its parameters from real data, starts from the state the real system is in now and forecasts from there; naga twin keeps one running beside a plant, scores its forecasts against what then happened and recommends among actions you name.
- [A plant as a timeline](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/plant-timeline.html): The views of a run (the HTML player, the debugger's inspection) draw one thing: the timeline a run's trace reduces to.
- [Live data](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/live-data.html): A model can read what a plant is saying right now: a REST service, an MQTT broker (plain topics or Sparkplug B), an OPC UA server or a Modbus TCP device.

## Coming from

- [SimPy](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/coming-from/simpy.html): Naga runs on SimPy: every block is a SimPy process and every resource a SimPy resource.
- [salabim](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/coming-from/salabim.html): salabim is a process-oriented simulation library: you write a class for each kind of thing that moves through the system, and its process method says what that thing does, one request, hold or release at a time.
- [Mesa](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/coming-from/mesa.html): Mesa is an agent-based modelling library for Python: an agent is a class, a model is a class that creates the agents, and by default time advances in steps in which each agent runs its step method (Mesa also has an experimental event scheduler).
- [Arena](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/coming-from/arena.html): The block vocabulary here is close to Arena's flowchart modules, and the expression functions keep the SIMAN names.
- [AnyLogic](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/coming-from/anylogic.html): Like AnyLogic, Naga runs discrete-event, system-dynamics and agent-based parts in one model on one clock.
- [Vensim](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/coming-from/vensim.html): Naga integrates stocks and flows on a fixed time step, with the functions a Vensim model uses most, and reads a .mdl file for a common subset of the language.
- [NetLogo](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/coming-from/netlogo.html): Naga has agents on a grid with patches, in continuous space or on a network, with links, ticks, births and deaths.

## Command line

- [Command line reference](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/cli/index.html): --help output of every naga command, captured live so it cannot drift from the real argument parsers, one page for each group of commands.
- [Run and compare](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/cli/run-and-compare.html): Run a model, compare scenarios and search for the best settings.
- [Check and edit model files](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/cli/model-files.html): Validate, format, diff, merge and test model files, and export them as code.
- [Build a model from data](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/cli/build-from-data.html): Draft a model from tables or an event log, or translate one from another tool.
- [Digital twin](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/cli/twin.html): Read a plant, start a run from its state, calibrate and forecast.
- [Plan, inspect and share](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/cli/plan-and-share.html): Plan with a solver, find the loops that drive a system dynamics model, and share a model in a browser.
- [Agents](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/cli/agents.html): Serve the model operations to an assistant.

## Blocks

- [Block reference](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/index.html): One page per block type, from nagasim/core/block_registry.py: what it does, its ports and parameters, the result frames it fills, the checks that name it, and an example that runs when the page is generated.
- [ASSIGN](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/assign.html): Sets attributes on a part, order or customer, or a model variable, from expressions as it passes, for example a due date, a type or a counter.
- [BATCH](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/batch.html): Groups parts or orders into batches, pallets or lots of a set size, or after a maximum wait, and sends the batch on as one entity.
- [BUFFER](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/buffer.html): Finite storage of waiting places between two machines or stations; when all places are taken the upstream machine stays blocked, holding its finished part.
- [CHARGE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/charge.html): Charges an entity (an electric vehicle, a battery pack) with the energy it needs at up to its own power, sharing a site power cap with every other entity at this block; it leaves when full or when its time is up.
- [CONVEYOR](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/conveyor.html): Conveyor belt that carries parts from one end to the other at a set speed, holds a limited number, and blocks the machine before it when full.
- [CREATE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/create.html): Source of arrivals: creates parts, orders, customers or jobs at random intervals or on an hourly arrival schedule.
- [DECIDE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/decide.html): Routing decision: sends each part, order or customer down one of several links by percentage chance, by a condition (rework, type, size) or by a policy.
- [DELAY](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/delay.html): Pure waiting time (transit, curing, travel, a pause) that holds the entity for a sampled duration without using any machine, operator or other resource.
- [DISPOSE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/dispose.html): End of the flow: parts, orders or customers leave the system here, and their throughput time and holding cost are recorded.
- [DUPLICATE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/duplicate.html): Makes copies of an entity, for example to model one job spawning several; the original goes on unchanged.
- [HOLD](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/hold.html): Holds entities waiting in a queue until a named signal fires, a condition becomes true (a buffer has room, a machine is idle), or for good.
- [LOGIC](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/logic.html): Custom routing written in Python: sends each entity to one of several outgoing links by your own rule when chance or a condition is not enough.
- [MATCH](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/match.html): Waits until one entity of each of several kinds is present (a part and its kit, an order and its customer), then releases them together.
- [MOTION](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/motion.html): Robot or cobot station whose service is a cycle of timed moves, picks, places and tool changes, so cycle time comes from motion data, not a distribution.
- [PROCESS](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/process.html): Machine, workstation or service step: a part, order or customer waits for a resource (machine, operator, server), is processed for a time, then frees it.
- [RECORD](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/record.html): Counts or measures something as entities pass (a count, a time between arrivals, a defect, a cost) in a user-named statistic, without delaying them.
- [RELEASE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/release.html): Frees a machine, operator or other resource that an earlier SEIZE gave the entity, after an optional delay.
- [ROUTE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/route.html): Sends a part or job to the next station on its own routing sequence (a job-shop or multi-step route) instead of along a fixed link.
- [SEIZE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/seize.html): Waits in a queue for a machine, operator, vehicle or other resource, takes it and keeps it until a later RELEASE, so one resource can span several steps.
- [SEND](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/send.html): Sends a message, with an optional payload, to agents of an agent-based model so they can react, for example a customer calling a driver.
- [SEPARATE](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/separate.html): Splits a batch, pallet or lot back into its individual parts, orders or customers, optionally copying the batch's attributes to each.
- [SIGNAL](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/signal.html): Broadcasts a named signal that releases every entity waiting at a HOLD block for it, for example a shift start, a gate opening or a green light.
- [STATION](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/station.html): Named stop on a job-shop or multi-step routing where a ROUTE block delivers parts, orders or jobs and sets their current location.
- [SUBMODEL](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/submodel.html): Editor-only blocks (SUBMODEL, SUB_ENTRY, SUB_EXIT) that group blocks into a reusable sub-model with named ports, expanded away before the run.
- [SUB_ENTRY](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/sub-entry.html): Editor-only blocks (SUBMODEL, SUB_ENTRY, SUB_EXIT) that group blocks into a reusable sub-model with named ports, expanded away before the run.
- [SUB_EXIT](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/sub-exit.html): Editor-only blocks (SUBMODEL, SUB_ENTRY, SUB_EXIT) that group blocks into a reusable sub-model with named ports, expanded away before the run.
- [TRANSFER](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/transfer.html): Adds to or takes from a continuous tank, stock or inventory level (fuel, material, a pool) as the entity passes, optionally waiting until it is available.
- [TRANSPORT](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/blocks/transport.html): Moves a part, order or load between locations with a vehicle (truck, AGV, forklift, robot) from a fleet: fetch, carry, unload, free the vehicle.

## Distributions

- [Distribution reference](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/index.html): One page per distribution, from nagasim/core/distributions.py's DISTRIBUTION_REGISTRY: its parameters, the mean and variance of seeded draws, a chart of the draws and an example.
- [Bernoulli](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/bernoulli.html): A single yes/no outcome with a given probability, such as accept or reject, pass or fail, or rework or not.
- [Beta](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/beta.html): A value between a minimum and a maximum with a flexible shape, such as a fraction, a proportion or a bounded time.
- [Binomial](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/binomial.html): Count of successes (for example defective parts) in a fixed number of independent trials.
- [BoundedNormal](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/bounded-normal.html): Bell-shaped variation around an average, cut off at a minimum and a maximum so a time cannot go negative or beyond a physical limit.
- [Cauchy](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/cauchy.html): Very heavy-tailed values with frequent extreme outliers in both directions; rarely right for times, and it often returns negative values.
- [ChiSquare](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/chi-square.html): Statistical diagnostics and sums of squared normal variations; rarely used for simulation times.
- [Constant](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/constant.html): A fixed duration that never varies, for a deterministic service time, transit time or interval.
- [CustomExpression](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/custom-expression.html): Any model expression, for example '2 + EXPO(3)', when no single distribution fits.
- [DiscreteUniform](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/discrete-uniform.html): A whole number between a minimum and a maximum, each equally likely, such as a random lot size from 1 to 6.
- [EmpiricalContinuous](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/empirical-continuous.html): Measured data as a histogram: a bin is picked by its weight, then a value is drawn evenly within it (a continuous draw, not a resample of points).
- [EmpiricalDiscrete](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/empirical-discrete.html): Whole-number values with their own measured probabilities, such as order sizes or the number of items per job.
- [Erlang](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/erlang.html): Time to finish k exponential steps in a row, giving a service time less variable than exponential but still random.
- [Exponential](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/exponential.html): Time between random independent arrivals, or time to a random breakdown, when past events do not change the next one.
- [FixedSchedule](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/fixed-schedule.html): Exact listed times, for arrivals or events that follow a fixed timetable such as a roster or a delivery plan.
- [Gamma](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/gamma.html): Right-skewed service or processing times that cannot go below zero, from very regular to very variable.
- [Geometric](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/geometric.html): Number of attempts until the first success, such as tries before a part passes inspection.
- [Hypergeometric](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/hypergeometric.html): Successes in a sample drawn without replacement from a finite lot, such as defectives found when inspecting a sample.
- [InverseGaussian](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/inverse-gaussian.html): Right-skewed positive times such as a reaction or decision delay, or the time for a drifting quantity to reach a level.
- [JohnsonSB](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/johnson-sb.html): A skewed value that stays between a minimum and a maximum, such as a yield or fill percentage.
- [JohnsonSU](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/johnson-su.html): A flexible fit for skewed, heavy-tailed data when no simple distribution matches; it can return negative values.
- [LogLogistic](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/log-logistic.html): Right-skewed durations with a heavier tail than lognormal, such as repair or lifetime data that cannot go below zero.
- [Lognormal](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/lognormal.html): Right-skewed times that cannot go below zero, such as manual handling, picking or repair durations with an occasional long one.
- [NegativeBinomial](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/negative-binomial.html): Number of failures before a set number of successes, each try with the same chance of success, such as rejected parts before r good ones.
- [Normal](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/normal.html): Symmetric variation around an average, such as a cycle time that is rarely far from the mean; it can go negative unless the mean is much larger than the spread.
- [PearsonTypeV](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/pearson-type-v.html): Right-skewed positive delays or times to failure with a long tail, an alternative to lognormal.
- [PearsonTypeVI](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/pearson-type-vi.html): A ratio of two gamma variables, such as cost per service, that is always positive; it can model times when the parameters suit.
- [Poisson](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/poisson.html): Counts per period, such as the number of arrivals or events in a fixed time window.
- [Rayleigh](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/rayleigh.html): A positive magnitude such as movement noise or a positioning error, with a single scale parameter.
- [Triangular](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/triangular.html): Min, most likely and max are known, usually from expert estimates when there is no data.
- [Uniform](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/uniform.html): Any value between a minimum and a maximum is equally likely; use it when only the min and max are known.
- [Weibull](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/distributions/weibull.html): Equipment lifetimes and time to failure, where the breakdown rate can rise with age (wear-out) or fall (early failures).

## Expression functions

- [Expression reference](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/index.html): core/expressions.py's grammar: a restricted-Python AST allow-list, never eval/exec.
- [Math](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/math.html): Plain arithmetic helpers, rounding and logic.
- [Trigonometry](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/trigonometry.html): Angles are in radians; DEG and RAD convert.
- [Random draws](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/random.html): Each call draws from the stream of the block (or agent) that evaluates it.
- [System dynamics](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/system-dynamics.html): Delays, smoothing, test inputs and finance for stock-and-flow models; most need simulation.sd.
- [Model state and lookups](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/model-state.html): Read an auxiliary, delay, level, flow, series, table, variable, conversion or the path network.
- [Resources and stores](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/resources.html): Queue, service and capacity of a resource, and a store's contents.
- [Arrays](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/arrays.html): Reduce a quantity over the elements of a subscript.
- [Agents and links](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/agents.html): Count and reference agents, and read an agent's links.
- [Agents in space](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/functions/agent-space.html): Neighbours, distances and patches of an agent on a grid or in a plane.

## Reference

- [KPIs](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/kpis.html): Every result frame nagasim.api.run_model / nagasim.experiments.run_scenarios return, and every column each one carries -- probed against nagasim/models/job_shop_jackson.json so a new KPI column fails this generation until it has a definition here.
- [Model file keys](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/schema.html): Current schema version: 29 (nagasim/core/schema/migrate.py).

## Model file sections

- [Model file sections](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/index.html): One page per top-level key of the model file, from the published JSON Schema (naga schema): what the key holds, each field with its type, default and unit, and an example fragment that the schema and the checks accept.
- [blocks](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/blocks.html): Every block in the model: name, type, position (centre, scene units), params.
- [links](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/links.html): Ordered list of {source, target, delay?, source_port?, target_port?}; array order is branch order, and several links may join the same pair of blocks (a link is identified by source, target and which of the parallel links it is).
- [scenarios](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/scenarios.html): Named parameter-override sets, run and compared by nagasim.experiments.
- [orders](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/orders.html): Released jobs with a due date, emitted by a CREATE block in "Orders" arrival mode.
- [resources](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/resources.html): Named resources: capacity, queue discipline, optional ranking expression, capacity schedule, cost fields.
- [resource_sets](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/resource_sets.html): Named groups of resources with a selection rule, seized as one pseudo-resource.
- [schedules](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/schedules.html): Piecewise-constant arrival-rate or capacity schedules, optionally repeating.
- [failures](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/failures.html): Resource failures: uptime/downtime distribution pairs per named resource group.
- [tables](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/tables.html): Named 1-D/2-D lookup tables read by TABLE("name", k1[, k2]) in any expression.
- [sequences](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/sequences.html): Named routings: ordered steps through STATION blocks, walked by a ROUTE block.
- [variables](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/variables.html): Model-level variables, read and written by expressions; reset to initial each replication.
- [entities](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/entities.html): Entity types: shape, colour, optional WIP holding cost.
- [timeseries_inputs](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/timeseries_inputs.html): Named time-series profiles read by TS("name") in any expression.
- [levels](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/levels.html): Continuous quantities with bounds (battery energy, tank volume, an inventory position), read by LEVEL("name").
- [flows](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/flows.html): Rate-based transfers between levels, re-evaluated at events.
- [conversions](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/conversions.html): Delayed conversions with a yield curve: feed in, product released over the following hours or days.
- [fixed_costs](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/fixed_costs.html): Costs of the scenario rather than of the run: capex (flagged capex: true for the investment case), or an annuity over a sized parameter.
- [fleets](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/fleets.html): Pools of vehicles that carry entities on the network; a fleet is a resource under its own name.
- [motion_profiles](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/motion_profiles.html): How robots, people and mechanisms move: speed, acceleration, payload derating and a collaborative speed, named by a MOTION block's profile.
- [zones](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/zones.html): Safety zones: a network node and a radius that a MOTION block's or a tending group's zone.name binds to; a worker inside slows the robot to its collaborative speed.
- [chargers](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/chargers.html): Chargers and battery-swap stations at network nodes, used by fleets that declare a battery.
- [auxiliaries](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/auxiliaries.html): Named expressions read by AUX("name"), evaluated on read.
- [delays](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/delays.html): Delays read by DELAY("name"): input, delay time, kind and order.
- [subscripts](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/subscripts.html): Dimensions: a record with "dims" is flattened into one record per element.
- [agent_types](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/agent_types.html): Statecharts run for every agent of a population: parameters, states, transitions.
- [populations](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/populations.html): Agent populations: a type, a count and an initial placement.
- [reality_checks](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/reality_checks.html): Vensim-style reality checks: a test input and a constraint the model must then satisfy.
- [network](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/network.html): Optional path network: nodes at layout coordinates and the segments joining them.
- [annotations](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/annotations.html): Text notes and frames drawn behind blocks on the canvas; ignored by the engine.
- [submodels](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/submodels.html): Reusable definitions (parameters, inner blocks/links/ports), flattened before a run.
- [background](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/background.html): Optional floor-plan image: path, position, scale, opacity, lock, real-world scale.
- [building](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/building.html): Optional building: rooms, walls, wall openings, floor markings, labels and plan fixtures in metres; the walls are the walled rooms' outlines and the free-standing wall lines, each with a height, thickness and finish.
- [info](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/info.html): Optional model metadata: description, author, notes; shown in the report header.
- [data_sources](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/data_sources.html): Declared CSV/Excel/SQLite/SQL/JSON sources model parameters can be read from.
- [data_bindings](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/data_bindings.html): Which column, filtered and transformed how, feeds which override path.
- [initial_state](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/initial_state.html): Warm start: entities already in blocks, variable values and resource states the run begins with.
- [simulation](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/simulation.html): Run settings: time_limit, warmup, replications, time_unit, currency, entity_log_limit, and the optional real-date calendar.
- [investment](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/investment.html): Optional investment case: the baseline scenario, horizon, discount rate, operating hours per year, margin per part and throughput KPI that naga invest compares every scenario with.
- [dispatch](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/dispatch.html): Optional storage dispatch plan: a rolling-horizon LP over the bus tags that drives every storage level marked optimal at the cheapest grid cost.
- [outputs](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/outputs.html): Optional extra output collection whose cost is opt-in, e.g.
- [assertions](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/assertions.html): Model assertions: a KPI, a comparison operator/value and a replication/confidence budget, checked by naga check.
- [path_checks](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/path_checks.html): Entity-path checks: rules on the blocks each entity visits (order, never, at most N times, always), checked by naga check on one traced replication.
- [dashboard](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/dashboard.html): Dashboard widgets: kpi/gauge/line/bar over the model's own expressions, sampled at the same instants as the timeseries sampler.
- [view](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/model-file/view.html): Editor view state: the canvas tab in front, layout/3D, zoom and centre per tab; written on save, ignored by the engine.

## Problem codes

- [Problem codes](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/index.html): The 464 codes that a check of a model can report, from nagasim/core/problems.py.
- [Agents](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/agents.html): Agent types, populations and their messages.
- [Submodels and libraries](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/submodels-and-libraries.html): Submodel definitions and instances, asset libraries and catalogues.
- [Data, live feeds and the twin](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/data-and-twin.html): Data sources and bindings, network access limits, live feeds, warm starts, saved states, plant mappings, the twin cycle and the MES.
- [Networks, fleets and automation](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/network-and-automation.html): Path networks, fleets, workers, motion, batteries and chargers, the investment case and the dispatch plan.
- [Expressions, stocks and flows](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/expressions-and-dynamics.html): Expressions and variables, tables and time series, levels, flows, conversions, conveyors, delays, subscripts and units.
- [Resources and time](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/resources-and-time.html): Resources and sets, schedules, failures, calendars and arrivals.
- [Scenarios, checks and the editor](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/scenarios-and-checks.html): Scenarios, assertions, path checks, dashboards, annotations and the file version.
- [Blocks, links and routing](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/reference/problems/blocks-and-flow.html): Blocks and their parameters, distributions, links, decisions, queues, routings and orders.

## Modelling guide

- [Modelling guide](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/index.html): How a model behaves, topic by topic: what each part of the model file means when it runs.
- [Entities and attributes](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/entities-attributes.html): An entity is the thing flowing through the model: a customer, a job, a part.
- [Expressions and variables](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/expressions-variables.html): A model file is data, not code.
- [Resources, sets and queues](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/resources-queues.html): A resource is a named capacity (e.g.
- [Schedules, failures and WAIT](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/schedules-failures.html): A Schedule is piecewise-constant: points = [[duration, value], ...], each value holding for duration time units, optionally repeating forever (without repeat, the last value holds forever once the points run out).
- [Units](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/units.html): Every quantity in a model names its unit: a duration, a length, a speed, a mass, an energy, a power or a rate per time.
- [Time units and transfer delays](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/time-units.html): simulation.time_unit (default "minutes") is the unit every KPI, the clock, the run length and the warm-up are expressed in, and the default unit of every new field.
- [Dates and calendars](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/dates-and-calendars.html): A model's clock is a plain number in the base time unit and always starts at 0.
- [Batching and matching](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/batching-matching.html): Groups entities by count only.
- [Submodels](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/submodels.html): A submodel is a reusable piece of model stored once, as a named definition, and used as many times as needed through a SUBMODEL instance block.
- [Costing](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/costing.html): Cost KPIs are computed at report time from the collectors every run already keeps -- costing adds no new simulation logic, only new columns on existing result frames.
- [Continuous quantities](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/continuous-quantities.html): Some things in a system are not entities.
- [Layout, paths and vehicles](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/layout-paths-vehicles.html): When distance matters -- a warehouse, a yard, a hospital corridor, an AGV aisle -- guessing a travel time is the weakest part of the model.
- [Finite buffers and blocking](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/finite-buffers.html): A queue in front of a station is unlimited unless you say otherwise.
- [Planning and scheduling](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/planning.html): An order book (the bundled model order_due_dates) answers "what happens if this shop runs".
- [Motion cycles](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/motion.html): A MOTION block is a station whose service is a cycle of motions.
- [Batteries and charging](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/batteries.html): An electric fleet can carry a battery, so a fleet-sizing study counts the time vehicles lose to charging.
- [Mobile cobots, machine tending](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/tending.html): A mobile cobot is a vehicle with an arm: it carries a part to a machine, puts it in, and later takes it out and carries it on.
- [Investment case](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/modelling-guide/investment.html): An investment case compares each scenario with a baseline and reports whether the extra capital pays for itself: payback, net present value (NPV) and return on investment (ROI).

## Background

- [System dynamics](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/system-dynamics.html): Stocks and flows with feedback, alongside the ordinary block flow chart -- the same model file, the same run_model.
- [Agent-based modelling](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/agent-based-modelling.html): Populations of agents, each running its own small statechart, alongside the ordinary block flow chart and system dynamics -- the same model file, the same run_model.
- [Security](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/security.html): A model file (.json) is untrusted data, exactly like a document someone emailed you.
- [Tools or code, an LLM case study](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/llm-study.html): The agent tools rest on a claim: a language model that builds a simulation through them gets a model that is valid, runs and gives the right answer more often than the same model writing SimPy code for the same request.
- [Stability and deprecation](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/stability.html): Before version 1.0 the Python API may change between minor versions, and every such change has a line in the release notes.
- [Contributing](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/contributing.html)

## Validation

- [Validation](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/validation/index.html): Naga is checked against answers that are known without simulating, and anyone can repeat the checks.
- [Reference models](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/validation/reference-models.html): Models whose answer is known exactly, from a formula found in the textbooks of the subject, beside what the engine gives when it runs them.
- [Benchmarks](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/validation/benchmarks.html): This page compares Naga with raw SimPy, salabim and Ciw on queueing models whose mean time in system is known exactly.
- [Citing](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/validation/citing.html): If Naga contributed to a paper, a thesis or a report, please cite it.

## Release notes

- [](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/changelog.html)
- [What's new](https://thematthub.github.io/naga/whats-new.html): This page gives the major changes of each minor release, newest first: what you can do now that you could not before, and what changes when you upgrade.
